key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine learning before device failure accelerates.
engineering_relevance: This enables a fast, non-invasive pre-screening tool for stability and quality control in scalable perovskite solar cell manufacturing, especially for tandem-ready films.
method: Nano-FTIR chemically identified impurity phases in perovskite films.
High-resolution reflected light microscopy captured impurity-rich regions over large areas.
Machine learning image analysis quantified harmful impurity density in seconds.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and degradation-tracking experiments showed that damage starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster at early stages.
watch_item: The diagnostic is promising, but it depends on reliable chemical validation and may need calibration across different perovskite compositions, processing routes, and imaging conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
